environment: Humpback whales turn up along the Queensland coast for their spring journey home
The Great Barrier Reef gears up for its annual coral spawning as water temperatures warm
science: Australian researchers trial a new reef-friendly sunscreen designed to protect coral while people swim
sports: Queensland footy fever builds as the Broncos and the Lions push deep into their respective finals series
stories.overview: Spring brings a wave of whale sightings and reef renewal along the Queensland coast

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, I'm Alex Mercer and it is a ripper of a Sunday, September the thirteenth. Spring's properly kicked in now, and honestly the vibe out there is pure Queensland magic. It really is, I'm Jamie and I've had my coffee on the balcony this morning just soaking it up. We've got a beauty of a show for you, whales, reefs, footy finals and a forecast from Sam that might just get you outside today. Too right. Grab a cuppa, settle in, and let's get into the good stuff happening around our state this week.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: Let's kick off the green segment because this one always gets me a bit giddy. Humpback whales are cruising past the Queensland coast right now on their way back south, and spotters reckon it's shaping up to be a cracking season. Yeah I love this time of year, you get families out on the headlands with binoculars just waiting for that big tail flick. It's one of those free shows nature puts on and Queensland's front row seat for it. And while the whales are doing their thing offshore, the Great Barrier Reef is gearing up for its big annual coral spawning event as the water starts to warm. Scientists say it's one of the best natural signs of a reef bouncing back and getting on with life.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Righto, science time, and this one's a beauty for anyone who loves a day at the beach. Aussie researchers have been trialling a new reef friendly sunscreen that's designed to protect your skin without harming the coral underneath. That's such a simple idea done well, because let's be honest, most of us just want to swim without feeling guilty about it. It's the kind of everyday science that actually changes habits, not just headlines. Exactly, and if it means healthier reefs for the kids and grandkids to enjoy later, that's a tick from me. Small bottle, big impact, that's the theme this week.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, thanks team. Right, south east Queensland, spring is well and truly strutting its stuff this week with plenty of sunshine and those classic clear blue skies we all love. Expect mild mornings warming into pleasant afternoons, so it's a great excuse to get outdoors, whether that's the beach, the hinterland or just the backyard. There's a gentle sea breeze keeping things comfortable along the coast, while it'll feel a touch warmer once you head inland away from that ocean influence. Keep an eye out for the odd fluffy cloud rolling through of an afternoon, but nothing to worry your barbecue plans. Back to you Alex and Jamie.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Sport time, and Queensland's footy tragics are living their best life right now with finals footy in full swing. The Broncos are grinding it out in the NRL finals series while the Lions keep the flag flying up north in the AFL, and the whole state's got that finals buzz. You can feel it everywhere too, the servos are selling out of jerseys and every second conversation at the shops turns into a footy chat. It's one of those times of year where Queensland really wears its heart on its sleeve. Couldn't agree more, win lose or draw, it's brought the mates together over a snag and a cold drink, and that's what footy's really about at the end of the day.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: Well that's about it from us today, what a lovely little wrap of good news to kick off the week. Whales offshore, reefs coming back to life and half the state glued to the footy. It really does remind you why we love calling Queensland home. There's always something worth smiling about if you know where to look. Big thanks to Sam for that gorgeous spring forecast, and to all of you for tuning in with us this morning. We reckon it's a top day to get outside and enjoy it. Couldn't have said it better myself. Get out there, soak up the sunshine, and we'll catch you all again tomorrow with more good news. Take care of yourselves and each other, this has been ParkSyde Bright Side, see ya tomorrow.
